title: Investigation-first observability matrix and trace playlist
content:
Summary:

This is a working plan for an "investigation-first" approach to observability for inference services. Goal: optimize dashboards and tracing for fast operator triage while keeping query/ingestion cost bounded. Focus is low-to-medium traffic models and multi‑tenant fanout routes where full sampling is expensive.

Why "investigation-first"?
- Many current dashboards prioritize high-level trending over the signals an oncall or SRE needs to answer "what broke and why".
- For inference, time-to-root-cause (TTRC) often dominates incident cost; we trade a little long-term retention for faster, higher-fidelity short-term investigation windows.

High-level approach (practical principles):
1) Prioritize signals that reduce search space quickly: session path, model variant, routing decision, cache hit, and token-rate spikes.
2) Keep cheap aggregated SLOs for long windows, but make detailed per-request traces and kv/cache events ephemeral and captureable on-demand.
3) Use a small decision matrix to decide which metrics to keep always-on, which to sample, and which to drop/prune.
4) Implement a "trace playlist" that operators can start that collects targeted high-fidelity spans for a rolling 30–90 minute window (short, dense capture).

Investigation Prioritization Matrix (simple scoring):
- Columns: Signal, Investigative Value (1–5), Query Cost (1–5), Retention Need (hours/days), Actionability (1–5), Keep/Save/Sample decision.
- Example rows (sample):
  - per-route 99th latency (InvestVal 5, Cost 2, Retention 30d, Action 5) => KEEP
  - per-tenant cold-cache-rate (4, 3, 14d, 4) => KEEP (plus alert)
  - kv-cache-miss-session-trace (5, 5, 12h, 5) => SAMPLE / TRACE-PLAYLIST
  - tokenized-attention-exceptions (5, 4, 7d, 5) => SAMPLE
  - per-batch-size histogram (3, 3, 7d, 3) => SAMPLE
  - per-request prompt-length distribution (2, 4, 7d, 2) => SAMPLE_LOW

Rules for scoring:
- Investigative Value: how often the signal reduces probable causes by >1 bucket.
- Query Cost: estimated QPS * cardinality weight * retention multiplier.
- Actionability: whether an alert/play can be run automatically or needs human action.
- Use thresholds to convert numeric score to policy: total >= 12 => KEEP, 8–11 => SAMPLE, <=7 => PRUNE/OFF by default.

Trace playlist concept (operator-driven):
- Intent: provide a quick toggle to collect higher fidelity traces for the next X minutes across specified dimensions (tenant(s), route(s), model(s), node pool).
- Default window: 30 minutes (configurable 15/30/60/120).
- Spans to capture at high fidelity: request start/end, runtime kernel selection, kv-cache lookup (prefix + hit/miss), routing decision logs, fallback model invocation, per-token generation slowdowns, and resource utilization snapshots (GPU utilization, mem pressure).
- Storage behavior: high fidelity traces are kept for a short retention (12–72 hours) then downsampled/rolled-up to span-level aggregates for long-term storage.
- Activation methods: console UI toggle, API call (observable trigger), incident runbook step, or automated based on thresholded anomaly (e.g., sustained 95th latency delta >30% for 5m).
- Playlist presets: "Canary regression" (captures canary route + model), "Tenant blowup" (captures single tenant across routes), "Cold cache sweep" (captures cache miss traces + associated KV keys).

Sampling heuristics and implementation notes:
- Adaptive sampling: keep baseline 0.5% of all requests as traces; when an anomaly is detected increase sampling multiplicatively for affected route/tenant for the next N minutes.
- Severity-weighted sampling: errors and high-latency requests get a higher sampling weight (e.g., 10x).
- Deterministic sticky sampling: if a request has the same session id as a sampled request in the last M minutes, sample subsequent requests to keep context.
- Cost cap: per-cluster / per-tenant sampling budgets (tokens of trace budget). If the budget is exhausted, fallback to metadata-only capture.

Dashboard notes (templates and panels):
- Investigation dashboard (operator home): narrow window (last 1h / 6h) with panels:
  - Top 10 routes by 95th latency (sparkline + anomaly delta)
  - Recent trace playlist toggle + status
  - Per-tenant error heatmap (tenant rows vs. error-type columns)
  - Cold-cache churn: misses per minute with correlated p95 latency overlay
  - Routing fallback rate: percent of requests that fell back to cheaper or older model
  - Query cost estimator panel: rolling estimate of query cost (tokens * pricing) with 24h lookback
- Longview dashboard (owners): 1d/7d trends, SLO burn rates, retention-aware aggregates. Keep cardinality low, avoid per-tenant panels unless high-volume tenant.
- Playbook widgets: inline links to incident runbook steps and to pre-filled trace playlist presets.

Metric definitions (short canonical list — operator-facing):
- route_request_count: count of requests to a logical API route (label: route, model_version, tenant)
- route_p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile server-side latency computed in streaming pipeline (labels as above)
- tenant_error_rate: ratio errors/total per tenant per minute (labels: tenant, error_class)
- cache_prefix_miss_rate: misses / lookups for prefix cache (labels: prefix_hash, route)
- fallback_rate_by_route: fraction of requests that invoked fallback model (labels: route, fallback_reason)
- batch_size_distribution: histogram of actual batch sizes at runtime (labels: node_pool, route)

Panel query advice (quick heuristics):
- Avoid joining high-cardinality tag sets in dashboard queries (tenant x route x model_version). Prefer single-dimension panels with quick drill links.
- Use fixed window quantiles in runtime dashboards (1m aggregation for 5m panels) to keep queries cheap.
- Precompute heavy aggregates (per-route percentiles) into a metrics rollup job instead of compute-on-read for long windows.

Ownership + alerting policy notes:
- Metric owners: assign one owner per high-cardinality metric (route_request_count, route_p95_latency_ms, fallback_rate_by_route). Owner is responsible for retention policy and query budget limits.
- Alerting: rely on SLO burn rather than raw p95 for noisy routes. For low-traffic models, use ratio-based alerts (e.g., p95 delta relative to 30d baseline) to avoid noise.

Practical implementation checklist (MVP):
- [ ] Implement trace playlist API + UI toggle (console) (owner: @Ethan)
- [ ] Baseline 0.5% sampling pipeline and severity-weighted multiplier (owner: @Ravi)
- [ ] Decision matrix spreadsheet (convert to config flags) (owner: Samira)
- [ ] Add operator investigation dashboard template (Grafana/Looker) with embedded preset buttons (owner: Lina)
- [ ] Add query-cost estimator panel and a per-cluster query budget alert (owner: infra-metrics)
- [ ] Run 2 tabletop drills using playlist presets to validate TTRC improvements (owners: eng-observability, sRE)

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- How long should premium traces be kept for customers on dedicated vs hosted tiers? (ops vs cost negotiation)
- Should trace playlist activation be allowed via infra-as-code for on-call automation? Risk: accidental long-term high-cost capture.
- How to standardize tenant cardinality caps across dashboards without cutting signal for small but important tenants?

Notes to self (working):
- Need a small RFC for the adaptive sampling algorithm (pseudocode + safety caps).
- Link to current sampling pipeline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/tree/main/sampling
- Related: Confluence page has long-term retention policy (confluence:OBS-2021-retention).

Appendix: quick pseudocode for adaptive sampling (sketch)
- baseline_rate = 0.005
- if anomaly_detected(route):
    sampling_rate(route) = min(0.2, baseline_rate * max_multiplier)
    start_timer(route, 15m)
- if error_status(request): weight = 10x
- enforce_budget(cluster, tenant): if budget_exhausted -> degrade to metadata-only mode

End notes: this is purposely terse and operator-focused. Next step: convert the matrix into a YAML config we can load into the metrics pipeline and prototype the playlist toggle in the console sandbox.

Comments welcome — drop feedback inline or ping #observability.
